small_guidance:
- The first GEMM is M=16384, N=4096, K=2048 — dominant cost. Add larger tile configs (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=32/64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4) and a GROUP_M=8 swizzle for L2 reuse across N tiles of a row group.
- Avoid the `wT = w.t().contiguous()` transposes (two extra full materializations of the weight matrices each forward). Load B directly from `w` using `stride_bk = w.stride(1)`, `stride_bn = w.stride(0)` — same data, no copy.
- In `gemm_lse_kernel`, increase BLOCK_N (e.g. 256) so the entire N=1024 row fits in 4 tiles with fewer K-loop restarts; also try num_stages=4 since K=4096 is large. Drop the per-tile `tl.where(-inf)` by handling the tail with a masked exp (write 0 directly) to reduce a select on the hot path.
large_guidance:
- Make the first GEMM (16384×4096×2048 → sigmoid) a persistent split-K-free GEMM with a tuned (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=32, GROUP_M=8) tile + fused sigmoid epilogue; this is the dominant operator and should approach cuBLAS throughput on the 4090.
- Consider fusing the entire second linear+LSE into a single persistent kernel where each program owns BLOCK_M rows and streams over N tiles of (hidden @ W2^T + b2), running online logsumexp in registers — already structurally present, but redesign so the K-loop is unrolled along a contiguous `hidden` row stored once in SMEM/regs and reused across all N tiles (cache the A tile across N iterations instead of reloading K=4096 elements per N tile).
- Pre-transpose both weights once in `__init__` (store W^T as a buffer) so forward never pays the transpose cost; current code re-transposes on every call.
